terms.grammar: noun, third declension, with a genitive
evidence: Cic. Agr. 2.76: orbis terrae pulcherrimus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Also orbis terrae, and in poetry orbis alone. “The finest in the world”: Cicero calls the land of Campania orbis terrae pulcherrimus.

terms.gloss: the universe; the world of men
evidence: Sen. Ep. 28.4: patria mea tōtus hic mundus est
terms.comment: Classically the ordered universe, the heavens, Greek κόσμος; in poetry and in Christian Latin the world and the people in it (Vulg. Jo. 8.12, ego sum lūx mundī).

evidence: Plaut. Rud. 465–470: ubi tū es gentium?
terms.comment: Not for the world, by no means: minimē gentium (Ter. Ad. 342).

phrases.latin: caelestēs ita velle ut mea Rōma caput orbis terrārum sit
phrases.english: (tell the Romans) that the gods wish my Rome to be the capital of the world

phrases.latin: ille terrārum mihi praeter omnīs angulus rīdet
phrases.english: that corner of the world smiles on me more than any other
where in the world are we?
the worst poet in the world

sources: Lewis & Short: orbis · Lewis & Short: terra · Lewis & Short: mundus · Lewis & Short: gens
